title: Compressor - isentropic efficiency, pressure ratio, off-design efficiency characteristic, inlet guide vanes
description: Residual eta_s*(h_out-h_in) = h_out,s-h_in with h_out,s from (p_out, s_in); specs pr/dp/P; off-design eta_s = eta_s,design*f(char line over m/m_design or pr) from a default characteristic line; igva angle shifts the characteristic. Power exchanged through PowerConnection (P = m*(h_out-h_in)).
notes: difficulty=easy; design equations map 1:1 to EES (one isentropic h_out,s call + efficiency equation); off-design needs a lookup table (data/char_lines.json 'Compressor DEFAULT'). reference results: yes (class docstring doctest: 50 l/s ambient air to 5 bar; tests/test_components/test_turbomachinery.py::test_Compressor). overlap: trivial block in every EES teaching set.

title: Turbocompressor - characteristic maps (pressure ratio and efficiency over corrected speed lines and mass flow), inlet guide vanes
description: 2D lookup maps char_map_pr and char_map_eta_s over non-dimensional mass flow and speed line, scaled to the design point; igva angle correction; default generic map in data/char_maps.json.
notes: difficulty=medium; needs 2D interpolation tables with design-point scaling. overlap: CoolSolve examples/turbocompressor.eescode and turbocompressor_interpolate.eescode already cover the map approach. reference results: yes (doctest + test_turbomachinery.py::test_TurboCompressor).

title: Turbine - isentropic efficiency, Stodola cone law and efficiency characteristic (DEFAULT / TRAUPEL lines) for off-design
description: Design: eta_s*(h_in-h_out,s) = h_in-h_out. Off-design: Stodola/cone law m = m_ref*(p_in/p_in,ref)*sqrt(v_ref*p_in,ref/(v*p_in))*sqrt((1-(p_out/p_in)^2)/(1-pr_ref^2)) and eta_s = eta_s,design*f(m/m_ref) from a lookup line (default or Traupel). Power through PowerConnection.
notes: difficulty=easy; three explicit equations (efficiency, cone law, char line) - cone law needs design-point values (m_ref, p_in,ref, v_ref, pr_ref) as constants of the off-design case. reference results: yes - doctest: 10 kg/s steam 550 C/110 bar -> 0.5 bar, eta_s=0.9 gives P=-10 452 574 W and x_out=0.914 (reproduced with CoolProp 7.2 during this sweep); off-design 28.8 t/h gives p_in=88.6 bar, eta_s=0.898; also tests/test_components/test_turbomachinery.py::test_Turbine. gap: Stodola law + char line off-design approach is rarely in EES teaching sets.

title: Steam turbine - wet-expansion efficiency correction (Baumann rule) with dry isentropic efficiency
description: eta_s = eta_s,dry*(1 - alpha*y_m) with mean wetness y_m = ((1-x_in)+(1-x_out))/2; for superheated inlet the code locates the saturation crossing (inner search) and applies the correction only to the wet part.
notes: difficulty=medium; the dry-to-wet crossing logic is an inner Newton search in Python -> in CoolSolve assume wet outlet (use average wetness) or add an IF on outlet quality. reference results: yes (doctest + test_turbomachinery.py::test_SteamTurbine). reference: Baumann rule (Traupel 2001, Thermische Turbomaschinen).

title: Pump - isentropic efficiency, head-flow characteristic (pressure rise vs flow), frequency scaling and efficiency maps
description: Options: eta_s; eta (hydraulic, incompressible flow work); flow_char: p_out-p_in = f(V_dot); head_flow_map and eta_flow_map as 2D maps over volumetric flow and frequency (affinity-law scaling of curves); eta_s_char off-design line; power via PowerConnection.
notes: difficulty=medium; curves/maps -> lookup tables (1D/2D). reference results: yes (doctest with maps + test_turbomachinery.py::test_Pump, test_Pump_maps, test_Pump_eta). overlap: LaboThapPy PumpCurveSimilarity (same affinity-law idea).

title: Positive-displacement compressor - EN12900 polynomial efficiency maps (Cecchinato et al. 2010)
description: Isentropic and volumetric efficiency as 10-coefficient EN12900 polynomials of evaporation and condensation temperature (reference state with given superheat/subcooling), coefficients optionally interpolated between compressor frequencies; swept volume x rpm gives mass flow, dissipation_ratio splits electrical power into heat loss; helper functions fit EN12900 coefficients from catalogue power/cooling tables (calc_EN12900, fit_EN12900, generate_eta_polys_from_data).
notes: difficulty=medium; polynomials are explicit; reference-state conversion (superheat/subcooling of catalogue) and the polynomial fit itself must be done outside (data preparation) or with a regression. reference results: yes (doctest + tests/test_components/test_polynomial_compressor.py with power/cooling catalogue tables; heat_pump_partload notebook with a Bitzer screw-compressor map). overlap: CoolSolve examples/orc_co2.eescode uses a polynomial compressor map (p00..p50).

title: Polynomial compressor with cooling-fluid heat recovery (oil/jacket cooling)
description: Extends the EN12900 compressor with a second fluid path recovering a share eta_recovery of the dissipated heat (energy balance on the cooling stream); tutorial for custom components.
notes: difficulty=medium; one extra energy-balance equation on top of the polynomial compressor. reference results: yes (doctest + tests/test_components/test_polynomial_compressor_with_cooling.py).

title: Counter-flow heat exchanger - energy balance, UA via smoothed LMTD, terminal temperature differences, pinch, effectiveness, pressure drop and UA characteristic lines
description: Hot-to-cold energy balance Q = m1*(h1,in-h1,out); optional specs: Q, kA/UA (Q + UA*LMTD = 0 with the robust Quoilin smoothed LMTD), ttd_u = T_in1 - T_out2, ttd_l = T_out1 - T_in2, ttd_min, td_pinch, eff_hot/eff_cold/eff_max (vs theoretical max enthalpy change), pr/dp/zeta per side; off-design UA = UA_design*f(m/m_design) via UA_char (DEFAULT, CONDENSING FLUID, EVAPORATING FLUID lines).
notes: difficulty=easy; explicit equations, no discretisation; careful with LMTD when dT_u = dT_l (use smoothed form) and with phase change inside the exchanger (single LMTD is wrong - use Condenser or sectioned models). reference results: yes (doctest + tests/test_components/test_heat_exchangers.py::test_HeatExchanger). robust LMTD is by S. Quoilin (PhD thesis 2011), CoolSolve already has an LMTD_F built-in.

title: Condenser - hot-side condensation with optional subcooling, upper terminal difference to saturation temperature
description: HeatExchanger variant for a pure condensing hot fluid: outlet saturated liquid (or subcooled by given amount), ttd_u defined against the dew-line temperature of the condensing fluid, UA characteristic for condensing fluid.
notes: difficulty=easy; use saturated-liquid enthalpy at the condensing pressure and an energy balance; for accurate UA with desuperheating/subcooling use a 3-zone or sectioned model. reference results: yes (doctest + test_heat_exchangers.py::test_Condenser, test_CondenserWithEvaporation).

title: Desuperheater - cools hot-side fluid to saturated vapour
description: HeatExchanger variant with hot outlet fixed at the dew state at the outlet pressure.
notes: difficulty=easy; reference results: yes (doctest).

title: Parallel-flow heat exchanger
description: Heat exchanger with co-current flow: LMTD built from inlet/outlet differences of the parallel arrangement; same specs as HeatExchanger (UA, ttd, pr).
notes: difficulty=easy; reference results: yes (doctest + test_heat_exchangers.py::test_ParallelFlowHeatExchanger*).

title: Heat exchanger - effectiveness-NTU with selectable flow arrangement (counter, parallel, crossflow variants, shell-and-tube n passes)
description: Q = eps(NTU, Cr, arrangement)*C_min*(T_hot,in-T_cold,in) with UA/NTU/eps/Q specs; capacity rates taken as effective values m*dh/dT between inlet and outlet states (C_r = 0 for an isothermal condensing/evaporating side); kA characteristics for off-design; relations calc_epsilon/calc_ntu for 7 arrangements, cross-validated against the 'ht' library and textbook values.
notes: difficulty=easy; closed-form eps-NTU relations as a FUNCTION with an arrangement flag (shell-and-tube/crossflow forms need care at Cr=0,1). reference results: yes and notably linked to this project - tests/test_components/test_ntu_heat_exchanger.py contains cases taken from CoolSolve examples (exchangers1: oil cooler UA=5000 W/K; exchangers2: crossflow gas/water heater; exchangers3: 2000 MW 1-2 shell&tube steam condenser) and a LaboThapPy HexeNTU case (Q=3961.9 W). overlap: CoolSolve examples/exchangers1-3 exist - value is the generalised arrangement function.

title: Sectioned (discretised) counter-flow heat exchanger - 51 enthalpy sections, UA by phase zone, Bell 2015 area constraint, Cecchinato UA scaling
description: HX split into N sections of equal heat duty (50 + extra sections at phase boundaries); per-section temperatures from (p,h) with linear pressure drop; UA per section from phase-dependent alpha values (area_zones, Bell 2015), td_pinch/ttd specs, robust LMTD per section (Quoilin 2011), UA_cecchinato part-load scaling, UA_char lines.
authors: Francesco Witte; Malte Fritz; Lennart Papa
notes: difficulty=hard; N-section arrays map to DUPLICATE (3 variables x N) but the section boundaries depend on phase (adaptive in code); a fixed-N version with explicit enthalpy grid is straightforward. reference results: yes (doctest with 17 reference values + tests/test_components/test_heat_exchangers.py, test_sectioned_hx_sc_phases.py; docs/how_to_guides/heat_exchangers.ipynb compares models). based on S. Quoilin's 'Next Generation Heat Pumps' discretisation (https://github.com/squoilin/NextGenerationHeatPumps) and the moving-boundary approach of Bell et al. (2015).

title: Moving-boundary heat exchanger (Bell 2015) - 3-zone/phase-boundary UA model
description: Subclass of the sectioned HX where sections are defined by phase changes (liquid/two-phase/vapour/supercritical on each side); UA_i = alpha-based zone conductances (alpha1_l/tp/g/sc, alpha2_*, area_ratio, R_cond); area_hot computed or specified (Bell area constraint); linear dp~dh assumption.
notes: difficulty=hard; zone boundaries and the set of active zones change with the operating point (IF-driven) - practical for a fixed regime (e.g. evaporator: liquid/2P/vapour on refrigerant side). reference results: yes - strong: tests/test_components/test_bell2015_oracle.py + bell2015_five_cases.json reproduce Bell's original HX.py oracle (Section A: water 330 K/0.1 kg/s vs n-propane 275 K/0.01 kg/s at 9.98 bar, constant alpha 100/1000 W/m2K, areas 0.2, 1, 2, 4, 7 m2 giving Q = 452 ... 4582 W with 1-3 cells; Section B: n-propane/n-propane, 3 cases with 3-5 cells; test tolerances 0.1 % on Q, 0.5 K on outlet T, 1 % on area). Bell, Quoilin, Georges, Braun, Groll, Horton, Lemort, Appl. Therm. Eng. 79 (2015). Same family as CoolSolve examples/condenser_3zones.eescode.

title: Simple heat exchanger (heat source/sink, consumer, pipe base) - Q/UA/ambient loss, Darcy-Weisbach or Hazen-Williams pressure drop
description: Single-stream component: Q = m*(h_out-h_in); optional Darcy pressure drop dp = 8*m^2*v*L*lambda/(pi^2 D^5) with Colebrook-type friction factor, Hazen-Williams, UA with ambient temperature and LMTD, pressure ratio/zeta.
authors: Francesco Witte; Jorrit Wronski; Hannes Schneider
notes: difficulty=easy; reference results: yes (doctest + test_heat_exchangers.py::test_SimpleHeatExchanger and UA convergence tests).

title: Pipe - Darcy-Weisbach pressure drop with surface or buried heat loss (insulation, wind, soil conduction)
description: SimpleHeatExchanger subclass: surface pipe heat loss from Gnielinski external convection + insulation resistance (wind_velocity, insulation_thickness/tc, material); buried pipe after Wallenten (1991) with pipe_depth and environment media; flow_speed spec; used for district-heating networks.
notes: difficulty=medium; heat-loss correlations (Gnielinski, Wallenten) are explicit but long; friction factor needs an implicit Colebrook or the explicit approximations. reference results: yes (doctest + tests/test_components/test_piping.py::test_Pipe).

title: Solar thermal collector - quadratic heat-loss model (Quaschning)
description: m*(h_out-h_in) = A*[E*eta_opt - lkf_lin*(T_m-T_amb) - lkf_quad*(T_m-T_amb)^2], T_m = (T_in+T_out)/2; optional Darcy pressure drop.
notes: difficulty=easy; one explicit equation (T_m depends on outlet -> implicit but trivial). reference results: yes (doctest + test_heat_exchangers.py::test_SolarCollector). reference: Quaschning, Regenerative Energiesysteme (2013).

title: Parabolic trough collector - efficiency with incidence-angle modifier and degree of cleanliness (Janotte 2014)
description: m*(h_out-h_in) = A*[E*eta_opt*doc^1.5*IAM - c1*(T_m-T_amb) - c2*(T_m-T_amb)^2], IAM = 1 - iam_1*|aoi| - iam_2*aoi^2; optional pressure drop.
notes: difficulty=easy; reference results: yes (doctest + test_heat_exchangers.py::test_ParabolicTrough; used in the SEGS validation model vs Ebsilon). reference: Janotte et al., Energy Procedia 49 (2014). overlap: LaboThapPy parabolic_trough_collector (different, semi-empirical model by Dickes/Lemort/Quoilin).

title: Valve - isenthalpic throttling with pressure ratio, zeta, Kv and opening characteristics
description: h_out = h_in; pressure drop by dp/pr, zeta (dp = (zeta/D^4)*8*m|m|*v_avg/pi^2, zeta/D^4 calibrated at the design point for off-design), Kv (Kv = V_dot*sqrt(rho/(1000*dp))), or Kv/dp characteristics over the valve opening (dp_char, Kv_char).
notes: difficulty=easy; reference results: yes (doctest + tests/test_components/test_piping.py::test_Valve*).

title: Drum / droplet separator - saturated liquid and vapour outlets of a two-phase inlet
description: DropletSeparator splits a single-fluid two-phase stream into saturated liquid and vapour; Drum additionally accepts a second inlet (circulation) for natural-circulation boilers (outlet states at saturation, mass/energy balance).
notes: difficulty=easy; saturation properties at the drum pressure. reference results: yes (doctest + tests/test_components/test_drum.py). used in the CGAM and SEGS models.

title: Mixing and splitting nodes - Merge, Splitter, Separator (fluid separation), Node
description: Merge: mass balance + enthalpy balance + composition mixing with pressure equality; Splitter: equal p,h,composition; Separator: splits fluid components with given fractions; Node: combined merge/split.
notes: difficulty=easy; reference results: yes (doctests + tests/test_components/test_merge.py, test_node.py, test_separator.py).

title: Combustion chamber - generic fuel/air stoichiometry, excess-air ratio lambda, thermal input, optional NOx; diabatic variant with heat loss and pressure drop
description: Complete combustion of a fuel mixture (CH4, C2H6, C3H8, C4H10, CO, H2, ... COMBUSTION_FLUIDS) with air to flue-gas composition (CO2, H2O, N2, O2, Ar, NO): mass balance per species, stoichiometry, energy balance with LHV (eta = heat-loss ratio in DiabaticCombustionChamber), lambda and ti (thermal input) specs, f_nox.
authors: Francesco Witte; Hannes Schneider; Jorrit Wronski
notes: difficulty=medium; fix the fuel (e.g. CH4) and write species balances explicitly; flue-gas properties via ideal-gas mixture of species (CoolSolve has ideal-gas CO2, H2O, N2, O2, CH4...); reference enthalpy/entropy conventions differ between tools (compare differences). reference results: yes (doctests + tests/test_components/test_combustion.py; CGAM and gas-turbine tutorial). overlap: CoolSolve examples/boiler_cpbar*.eescode, internal_combustion_engine*.eescode.

title: Combustion engine (CHP) - thermal input to power/heat/loss via characteristic lines, two heating ports
description: Gas-engine cogeneration: combustion stoichiometry as in CombustionChamber; electrical power P = f_tiP(ti/ti_design)*ti, heat to port 1 and 2 (Q1_char, Q2_char) and heat loss (Qloss_char) from default characteristic lines; mechanical efficiency; four fluid ports (air, fuel, cooling water 1/2, exhaust).
authors: Francesco Witte; Jorrit Wronski; Karim Shawky
notes: difficulty=medium; characteristic lines -> lookup tables (data/char_lines.json 'CombustionEngine DEFAULT'). reference results: yes (doctest + test_combustion.py::test_CombustionEngine). gap: CHP gas-engine block with load-dependent characteristics.

title: Water electrolyzer - hydrogen/oxygen production with efficiency characteristic and heat recovery
description: Power-to-gas: specific energy consumption e, efficiency eta (= LHV/HHV based), heat output and cooling-water energy balance, gas outlet temperature; eta_char off-design line; reference temperature 298.15 K, 1 bar.
authors: Francesco Witte; Benjamin W. Portner; Jorrit Wronski
notes: difficulty=medium; species flows per electrochemistry (H2O -> H2 + 1/2 O2) plus energy balance with formation enthalpies. reference results: yes (doctest + tests/test_components/test_reactors.py).

title: Fuel cell - H2 + O2 -> H2O with efficiency, power and heat output
description: Electrochemical conversion: P = eta*(-dH_reaction)*m_H2 (specific energy e), heat output via cooling water, gas/water outlets from mass balance.
notes: difficulty=medium; reference results: yes (doctest + tests/test_components/test_reactors.py::test_FuelCell).

title: Motor / Generator / PowerBus / HeatBus - efficiency (optionally load-dependent) and energy-flow balances
description: Converters with eta (and optional characteristic over normalised output), power balance on buses (sum in = sum out), heat bus analogue; used to track net electrical output.
notes: difficulty=easy; one-line equations. reference results: yes (doctests).

title: Humid-air connection - psychrometric state (w, relative humidity, enthalpy of humid air) for cooling coils
description: Experimental HAConnection wrapping CoolProp HumidAir: dry-air mass flow as the conserved quantity, humidity ratio w or relative humidity r, condensate flow; used with MovingBoundaryHeatExchanger as dehumidifying coil.
authors: Francesco Witte; Jorrit Wronski; Jacob Østergaard Pedersen
notes: difficulty=medium; CoolSolve already has built-in psychrometric functions (HumRat, RelHum, PsychProps) and examples cooling_coil/humidair1-2/evaporator. reference results: no (how-to notebook has no stored outputs).

title: Darcy friction factor (laminar 64/Re, Blasius, Filonenko, Colebrook) and Hazen-Williams pressure drop
description: darcy_friction_factor(Re, ks, d): 64/Re (Re<=2320), smooth-pipe correlations 0.03164*Re^-0.25 / (1.8*log Re - 1.5)^-2 and implicit Prandtl-Colebrook forms; Hazen-Williams dp = 10.67*m^1.852*L/(k^1.852*d^4.871) in simple.py.
notes: difficulty=easy; Colebrook part is an implicit equation (natural in CoolSolve). reference results: no dedicated test values (used in Pipe/SimpleHeatExchanger tests). overlap: CoolSolve examples/pressuredrop.eescode (Colebrook-White).

title: Smoothed LMTD (Quoilin 2011) - continuous log-mean temperature difference for zero/negative terminal differences
description: smoothed_lmtd(dTa,dTb): standard LMTD above threshold eps, linear extrapolation with slope xi below it, average when dTa=dTb; makes UA equations differentiable through temperature crossings.
notes: difficulty=easy; one FUNCTION with IF branches. reference results: indirect (UA tests). Authored from S. Quoilin's PhD thesis (2011, https://hdl.handle.net/2268/96436). note: CoolSolve LMTD_F already has a smooth limit at dT1=dT2; the extension to negative differences is the difference.

title: Effectiveness-NTU relations for 7 flow arrangements: calc_epsilon, calc_ntu
description: counterflow, parallelflow, crossflow (both unmixed approximation, one mixed, both mixed), shell-and-tube with n shell passes; inverse relation calc_ntu(eps, Cr).
notes: difficulty=easy; reference results: yes - textbook identities + cross-validation against the 'ht' library in tests/test_components/test_ntu_heat_exchanger.py (round-trip tests, Cr=0 collapse). Ready-made FUNCTION library; complements LaboThapPy correlations/heat_exchanger/e_NTU.py.

title: Default off-design characteristic lines (turbine, compressor, pump, heat-exchanger UA, CHP engine, electrolyzer) and compressor map
description: Lookup tables x/y for Turbine eta_s_char (DEFAULT, TRAUPEL), Compressor/Pump eta_s_char, HeatExchanger/Condenser/Pipe UA_char/kA_char (DEFAULT, CONDENSING FLUID, EVAPORATING FLUID), CombustionEngine tiP/Q1/Q2/Qloss, WaterElectrolyzer eta_char; char_maps.json holds the generic TurboCompressor maps.
notes: difficulty=easy; copy as CoolSolve lookup tables (CSV) with linear interpolation. reference results: n/a (data). Traupel line from Traupel, Thermische Turbomaschinen (2001).

title: Heat-exchanger UA part-load scaling after Cecchinato et al. (2010): f_UA from mass-flow ratios and Reynolds exponents
description: f_UA = (1 + x)/((m_cold/m_cold,ref)^(-Re_cold) + x*(m_hot/m_hot,ref)^(-Re_hot)) with x = (alpha_cold/alpha_hot)*(A_cold/A_hot); equation 0 = UA_ref*f_UA - sum(UA_i) over the sections (groups UA_cecchinato / UA_cecchinato_hc with re_exp_hot, re_exp_cold, alpha_ratio, area_ratio); used for off-design heat pumps and chillers.
authors: Francesco Witte; Malte Fritz; Lennart Papa
notes: difficulty=easy; explicit scaling with design-point constants. reference results: yes (tests/test_components/test_heat_exchangers.py::test_*_offdesign_cecchinato_*; heat_pump_partload notebook). reference: Cecchinato, Chiarello, Corradi, Int. J. Thermal Sci. 49 (2010) 1776.

title: Physical (thermo-mechanical) exergy of a state and exergy-splitting helpers
description: calc_physical_exergy(h,s,p,pamb,Tamb): e_ph = (h-h0) - T0*(s-s0) with ambient reference state, two-phase splitting into thermal and mechanical parts; exergy analysis proper moved to the external 'exerpy' package.
notes: difficulty=easy; one FUNCTION (reference state at T0,p0). reference results: yes (CGAM and SEGS tests include exergy balance checks via exerpy; sCO2 notebook lists published thermal/mechanical exergies).

title: Rankine cycle with cooling-water condenser, generator/motor, parametric study and part load (cone law)
description: Superheated steam cycle: 10 kg/s at 600 C/150 bar, condenser 0.1 bar (or ttd_u=4 K), steam generator pr=0.9, eta_s turbine 0.9 and pump 0.75, cooling water 20->30 C; then generator/motor efficiencies and net power spec, parametric sweeps (live-steam T/p, cooling T), design/off-design with Stodola cone law and UA.
notes: difficulty=easy; ~25 state equations (turbine, pump, condenser balance with cooling water, steam generator). reference results: no stored numbers in the repo (tests only execute the script); independent CoolProp 7.2 check from the tutorial specs (first solve, no generator/motor): P_turbine=13.21 MW, P_pump=0.224 MW, Q_sg=33.69 MW, eta_cycle=38.6 %, x_out=0.866 - computed here, not from TESPy. overlap: CoolSolve rankine1/rankine2 examples (60 MW) - this adds the cooling-water coupling and part-load logic.

title: Simple heat pump (R134a): compressor, condenser, valve, evaporator with parametric COP studies
description: R134a, condenser heat output 1000 kW, evaporation 20 C (sat. vapour), condensation 80 C (sat. liquid), eta_s=0.85, 2 % pressure drop in both HX; variants: fixed mass flow, pressure ratio spec, discharge temperature spec; COP vs source/sink temperature and eta_s.
notes: difficulty=easy; ~12 equations. reference results: no stored numbers; independent CoolProp 7.2 check from the specs: p_evap=5.72 bar, p_cond=26.87 bar, T_discharge=91.2 C, COP=3.378, m=8.06 kg/s, P_comp=296 kW (computed here, not from TESPy). overlap: CoolSolve refrigeration1-3, compressor_refrigeration_simple.

title: Open gas-turbine cycle with combustion chamber (CH4/CO2 fuel), generator and parametric studies
description: Compressor (pr=15, eta_s=0.85), diabatic combustion chamber (lambda=1.5 first, eta=0.98, pr=0.97, fuel 96 % CH4/4 % CO2), turbine (eta_s=0.9, TIT 1200 C), generator 0.98; efficiency vs TIT and compression ratio; fuel composition and flue-gas O2 specification variants.
notes: difficulty=medium; species balances for combustion + ideal-gas mixture enthalpies; otherwise a standard Brayton loop. reference results: no stored numbers (tests execute the script only); CGAM test model (see row) provides validated numbers for the same building blocks. overlap: CoolSolve cpbar/boiler examples; gas-turbine Brayton teaching models.

title: District heating loop: heat source, feed pump, consumer, valve, feed/return pipes with pressure drop and heat loss
description: INCOMP::Water loop at 90/65 C and 10-13 bar: consumer heat load, pipes with roughness 0.5 mm and length 100 m (diameter as variable), UA heat loss to ambient (Tamb=0 C), parametric studies of ambient temperature, load and temperature level.
notes: difficulty=easy; ~20 equations; Darcy friction factor implicit (Colebrook). reference results: no stored numbers (tests execute the script). gap: district-heating pipe network with heat loss is absent from CoolSolve examples.

title: NH3 heat pump with two-stage compression and intercooler, built step by step (consumer, valve/evaporator, compressors)
description: Ammonia heat pump delivering 230 kW to a water consumer circuit; evaporator (dew-point superheating), intercooler between two compressors, subcooling and pinch specs (td_pinch=10 K, ttd_l=5 K); finally switched to design/off-design with efficiency characteristics.
notes: difficulty=medium; ~40 equations; spec switching (dew temperatures vs pinch) is tutorial content, not model physics. reference results: no stored numbers. overlap: CoolSolve heat_pump_MSTh_SB_R10 and refrigeration examples.

title: R290 heat pump with internal heat exchanger, heat-source loop and consumer loop (solver starting-value tutorial)
description: Refrigerant cycle with evaporator fed by a heat-source pump loop, IHX, condenser feeding a consumer cycle; used to demonstrate starting-value selection.
notes: difficulty=easy; same topology family as the basic heat-pump rows. reference results: no. mostly solver documentation.

title: Regenerative steam power plant with two feedwater preheaters (HP/MP/LP turbines) - extraction-pressure optimisation
description: Steam generator, HP/MP/LP turbines with two extraction splitters, condenser, feed pump, two closed feedwater preheaters (one with a desuperheater) with drain pumps and merges (14 main-cycle + 7 preheating connections); ModelTemplate + pymoo differential evolution maximises cycle efficiency over the two extraction pressures.
notes: difficulty=medium; base plant (~14 state points, 3 turbines, 2 heaters, 3 pumps) is directly translatable for given extraction pressures; the DE optimisation is not (no optimiser in CoolSolve - replace by a 2-D parametric sweep). reference results: no stored numbers. overlap: CoolSolve rankine2 (one extraction) - this is the two-extraction extension.

title: Ground-coupled heat pump (NH3/R290) with exergy analysis - compressor, MB condenser/evaporator, valve, collector and heating loops
description: ModelTemplate class: refrigerant cycle with moving-boundary heat exchangers, ground-source brine loop (9.5 C), underfloor heating (40 C), compressor/pump with motors and characteristics; exergy analysis (exerpy) with COP and exergetic efficiency vs ambient/geothermal temperature and refrigerant.
notes: difficulty=medium; the thermal model is translatable; the exergy post-processing needs a reference-state exergy FUNCTION (see physical exergy row). reference results: partial (figures only; tests/test_heat_pump_exergy.py checks execution/results). reference data from a Viessmann Vitocal 300-G datasheet (approximate).

title: Supercritical CO2 recompression Brayton cycle with two recuperators (100 MW net), validated against published data
description: Cycle: turbine (600 C/250 bar in, eta_s), main and re-compressor, two sectioned recuperators (10 sections), water cooler, heater, split/merge; motors/generator efficiencies; published temperature/pressure/exergy table for 12 listed states (labels 1-6 and 10-15; Penkuhn & Tsatsaronis 2018); sensitivity analyses (TIT, compressor inlet T/p, split ratio, recuperator pinch) and NSGA-II optimisation (efficiency vs UA).
notes: difficulty=medium; ~13 state points, 2 compressors, 2 recuperators (use 10-section DUPLICATE or specify pinch/effectiveness), smooth CO2 properties near the critical point help convergence; the optimisation part is out of scope (replace with parametric sweeps). reference results: yes - strong: published table of T, p, thermal and mechanical specific exergy for the 12 listed states (e.g. state 1: 35.00 C/75.00 bar, state 4: 600 C/250 bar, state 5: 456.95 C/77.95 bar) embedded in the notebook; TESPy deviations are near zero for T and p. Source: Penkuhn & Tsatsaronis (2018), 6th Int. Symp. sCO2 Power Cycles; model from Witte et al. 2022 exergy paper (github.com/fwitte/sCO2_exergy). overlap: CoolSolve orc_co2 is a CO2 ORC, not a recompression Brayton cycle.

title: Combined-cycle power plant with district-heat extraction (300 MW electricity + 100 MW heat): gas turbine, HRSG, steam cycle
description: Gas turbine with HRSG (economiser/evaporator/superheater with drum and pinch/approach specs), extraction-condensing steam turbine providing district heat, condenser; ModelTemplate with staged solving; QT diagram of HRSG, sensitivity (live-steam pressure 30-110 bar, pinch, TTD) and PSO optimisation.
notes: difficulty=hard; ~100 state variables, drum + HRSG sections, staged specification switching needed for convergence. reference results: partial (originates from the exerpy combined-cycle example, modelled in Ebsilon there; no stored numbers in this repo). gap: combined-cycle with heat extraction.

title: CO2 transcritical booster refrigeration system (supermarket): LT/MT evaporators, receiver, flash gas, gas cooler, heat recovery
description: Booster cycle with LT and MT compressors, gas cooler (subcritical 57.3 bar case and transcritical 100 bar case), high-pressure valve, receiver at 32 bar, MT/LT evaporators at 26/13 bar, heat-recovery heat exchanger; COP = (Q_LT+Q_MT)/(P_LT+P_MT); sensitivity of COP to gas-cooler pressure and PSO of gas-cooler and receiver pressure.
notes: difficulty=medium; ~25 state points; supercritical gas-cooler states and near-critical receiver need good initial values. reference results: yes - Case Study 1 table of the source chapter is embedded (LT 13 bar/25 kW, MT 26 bar/75 kW, receiver 32 bar, gas cooler 57.3 bar/15 C, eta_s,LT=0.85, eta_s,MT=0.80) but result values are not stored; source: D'Ettorre & Heerup, 'Modelling of a commercial refrigeration system in Python' (book chapter, 2026) - cite when reused. overlap: CoolSolve refrigeration examples (single stage); CO2 booster is new.

title: Water-to-water heat pump with IHX and screw compressor map (EN12900 polynomials): design at 300 kW and part-load frequency sweeps
description: Cycle with polynomial compressor fitted to a BITZER SP-111-1 catalogue (30/50/90 Hz tables transposed to isentropic/volumetric efficiency polynomials), condenser/evaporator with UA scaling after Cecchinato (2010), IHX; design (12->7 C source, 30->40 C sink, pinch 5 K, 5 K superheat) and off-design sweeps over frequency, sink and source temperature.
notes: difficulty=hard; needs the compressor polynomial fit data (catalogue tables) and design-state constants for the UA scaling; frequency interpolation of coefficients. reference results: partial (catalogue-derived inputs; no stored outputs). BITZER catalogue data cited from vendor documentation - check redistribution terms before copying tables.

title: Recuperated, preheated ORC (isopentane) with air-cooled condenser, and a two-cycle cascade heat pump with internal heat exchanger
description: ORC: turbine (eta_s 0.8), recuperator, condenser (air, pinch 5 K), pump (0.7), preheater and evaporator (moving-boundary HX, pinch 10 K), air heat source 200 C/10 kg/s, generator/motor 0.98, net power spec; second model: low/high-temperature refrigerant cycles coupled by an IHX with COP target (user-defined equation).
notes: difficulty=medium; ORC ~15 state points with MB heat exchangers (3 zones) - fix the zone topology per exchanger. reference results: no stored numbers. overlap: CoolSolve orc_simple/orc_complex (generic) - novelty: air-cooled condenser, preheater+evaporator with brine/air source and pinch design specs; same ORC used in advanced_debugging.ipynb.

title: Heat-exchanger model comparison: condensation of a working fluid with HeatExchanger, Condenser, MovingBoundary and Sectioned models
description: Same condensing-fluid problem solved with four HX models, effect of number of sections, pressure drop, preheating towards saturation and supercritical isobar curvature; QT diagrams and results table.
notes: difficulty=easy-medium; a ready-made verification set for translated HX models (no stored outputs; run TESPy to obtain tables). reference results: no stored outputs in the notebook.

title: Cooling coil with humid air: humidity ratio or relative humidity at the inlet, condensate formation
description: Air at 15 C/1 bar with w=0.004 kg/kg (or r=0.9) cooled to 5 C in a moving-boundary coil; reports dry-air flow, humid-air flow and condensate (390 g/s case).
notes: difficulty=medium; CoolSolve has psychrometric built-ins and cooling_coil.eescode - low added value. reference results: no stored outputs (one number in the text).

title: Zeotropic-mixture heat pump (propane/isobutane, propane/pentane): temperature glide, COP and VHC vs composition
description: Heat pump with SectionedHeatExchanger condenser/evaporator and a mixture working fluid; Thermopack (cubic EoS) vs REFPROP engines; composition sweep 0-100 % propane; QT diagrams show glide matching.
notes: difficulty=hard; needs mixture bubble/dew properties (CoolProp HEOS mixtures are less robust; REFPROP back end optional). reference results: yes in notebook outputs (6 cells with stored outputs) but engine-specific. out of scope for a first library wave.

title: CGAM cogeneration problem: gas turbine with air preheater, HRSG (economiser/evaporator/drum) - benchmark vs Ebsilon
description: Compressor (pr=10, eta_s=0.86), air preheater (air heated to 850 K), diabatic combustion chamber (eta=0.98, pr=0.95, CH4), gas turbine (TIT 1520 K, eta_s=0.86), HRSG delivering 14 kg/s of saturated steam at 20 bar (drum, evaporator, economiser outlet 15 K below saturation), 30 MW net power; exergy analysis with chemical exergy (exerpy).
notes: difficulty=medium; classic cogeneration benchmark (CGAM problem, Valero et al. 1994) - ~12 states; combustion species balance + ideal-gas flue gas. reference results: yes - tests/test_models/cgam-ebsilon-results.csv lists m, T, p, h, s and molar composition for states 1-10, 6p, 8p plus compressor power 29.66 MW and turbine power -59.66 MW (agreement < 0.5 %); the TESPy validation page also states a comparison with literature data (Valero et al. 1994, Energy 19(3); Bejan et al. 1996) - the exact input set of this test (pr=10, 30 MW) should be checked against the textbook case before comparing. gap: CGAM absent from CoolSolve examples.

title: SEGS parabolic-trough solar power plant (Therminol VP-1 field, superheater/evaporator/economiser/reheater, 7 turbine stages, 5 feedwater heaters, cooling tower) - benchmark vs Ebsilon
description: Solar field (ParabolicTrough, Therminol VP-1 at 390 C, 23.3 bar) heating a Rankine cycle with drum boiler, reheater, 2 HP + 5 LP turbine stages with extraction splitters, 3 LP + 2 HP condensing preheaters with sub-coolers, condenser with a cooling tower (modelled as air/water heat exchanger with fan); full generator/motor power chain.
notes: difficulty=hard; ~80 fluid connections and 25 power flows with individually specified stage efficiencies (0.64-0.94) and pressure levels; needs Therminol VP-1 properties (incompressible oil data; may need a table/correlation in CoolSolve). reference results: yes - Ebsilon: net power 31.769 MW (rel. tol 5e-4) and temperature at connection 79 (solar-field inlet) = 296.254 C (abs 0.05 K) asserted in the test; model originates from github.com/fwitte/SEGS_exergy (Witte et al., Energies 2022).

title: Two-stage NH3 heat pump with flooded evaporator (drum + circulation pump), superheater and intercooler - off-design COP vs Ebsilon
description: Condenser (60 bar NH3, 60->105 C water), valve, drum with evaporator pump loop, evaporator + superheater on a 12 C water source, two compressors with intercooler (15 bar), characteristic lines for compressors/pump/HX; off-design COP matrix over sink temperature (80-105 C) and source mass flow (10-33 kg/s).
notes: difficulty=hard; off-design with design-state parameters and characteristic lines; ~40 state points. reference results: yes - Ebsilon COP table 4 sink temperatures x 5 source flows (2.216-2.866) with 7 % tolerance (not all Ebsilon characteristics available - perfect match impossible, as stated in the test).
